I compared it with the other users of the same API. `RestrictedStdReduction.lean` has a near-identical block in `le_layer_of_isComponentOf_centralizer`. I read the lemma `kProper_solvable_odd_quotient_ordinary_local_image_enters_two_layer` that both call. I also checked the imports: `RestrictedStdReduction` already imports `KProperSolvableOddQuotientLayer`, so the shared lemma could live there. Other files use `isComponentOf_map_iff` and `map_centralizer_singleton_of_injective`, but with different embeddings, so I did not count them as repeats. The rewrites were not compiled. findings.problem: The first half of the proof is repeated in `le_layer_of_isComponentOf_centralizer` in `RestrictedStdReduction.lean`. Both proofs build the trivial-kernel `QuotientGroup.mk' ⊥` injectivity fact `hinj`. Both transport a component of `centralizer {t}` to a component of `centralizer {mk' ⊥ t}` in `H ⧸ ⊥` (`himage`), using `isComponentOf_map_iff`, `map_centralizer_singleton_of_injective`, `range_eq_top` and `top_inf_eq`. Both extract perfectness from `isQuasisimple_iff_native`, discharge `Odd (Nat.card ⊥)`, and call `kProper_solvable_odd_quotient_ordinary_local_image_enters_two_layer` to get `J ≤ pLayer H 2`. The reasoning is about 10 lines of nontrivial group and component transport, copied nearly verbatim and not shared. A fix to one copy would have to be made in the other.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to `kProper_solvable_odd_quotient_ordinary_local_image_enters_two_layer` in `KProperSolvableOddQuotientLayer.lean`, which both files already import:

theorem kProper_ordinary_local_component_le_two_layer {C : CFSG.Assembly.GroupProp} (hS : SchreierFor C) {G : Type} [Group G] [Finite G] (hK : CFSG.Assembly.KProper C G) {t : G} (ht : orderOf t = 2) {J : Subgroup G} (hJ : CFSG.Assembly.IsComponentOf J (centralizer ({t} : Set G))) : J ≤ CFSG.pLayer G 2

The proof is the current lines 16–26 verbatim: `hinj`, `himage`, `hJp`, then the call with `N := ⊥` and `odd_one`.

Rewrite this theorem as `have hJ2 : J ≤ CFSG.pLayer H 2 := kProper_ordinary_local_component_le_two_layer hS hK ht hJ`, followed by the existing `hpl`, `hJE` and the orbit-location part.

Rewrite `le_layer_of_isComponentOf_centralizer` as `exact (kProper_ordinary_local_component_le_two_layer hS (kProper_of_isKGroupCat' hK) ht hJ).trans (sSup_le fun Q hQ => le_sSup (isComponent_of_isPComponent_two hO hQ))`.

The `hO` and `isComponent_of_isPComponent_two` step stays local, since it differs between the two files.
findings.benefit: This removes about 10 duplicated lines of component and quotient transport from each caller. The statement 'a component of an involution centralizer lies in the 2-layer under KProper' gets a name and a single proof. Both callers become short and keep only their own steps: orbit location here, and the `isComponent_of_isPComponent_two` step in the other file. If the trivial-quotient bookkeeping changes, only one proof needs updating.

evidence.excerpt: hS (kProper_of_isKGroupCat' hK) ⊥ (by rw [Subgroup.card_bot]; exact odd_one) ht hJ.1 hJp
